scope: Only the six named decisions and associated context/rationale fields may change; the other fifteen decisions and all audit/identity/order fields stay identical. No scores or critique changes. One same-context unsaved reconsideration, no saved retry.

findings.label: Argument from ignorance
findings.issue: Rationale invents asserted failure to disprove a creator; the source claims a beginning, distinguishes vacuum from nothing, criticizes rival models and explicitly frames a best-explanation inference. Reconsider exact absence-of-proof definition versus underdefended comparative explanation. If retained, identify the actual source transition satisfying the definition without inventing failure-to-disprove language.

findings.label: Ambiguity effect
findings.issue: Source explicitly grants this is an explanation one might propose and asks whether it raises more questions. Lack of contradiction or exclusion does not establish preference for a clearer option. Identify actual preference satisfying definition, or reject; do not turn comparative withholding into a claim of disproof.

findings.label: Appeal to authority
findings.issue: Craig reports a philosopher’s argument, gives expected-versus-unexpected consciousness reasoning and identifies best explanation. Sparse support and citation alone do not establish reliance on status as settling. Identify actual status substitution distinct from unsupported premises. Avoid uncertain proper names as a basis.

findings.label: Ambiguity effect
findings.issue: Source asks how agency causes, why it is a better explanation than randomness, and whether mystery is reduced. Rationale asserts preference for a clearer brute origin beyond those questions. Distinguish methodological explanatory challenge from preference based on ambiguity; lack of refutation is not itself the bias.

findings.label: Argument from ignorance
findings.issue: Source explicitly offers three affirmative facts and a cumulative historical inference, with some comparison of alternatives. Omitting stronger alternatives is not automatically ignorance. Identify actual absence-of-proof inference distinct from incomplete comparison, and ensure it is distinct from the authority candidate.

findings.label: Red herring
findings.issue: Final reply answers Christianity’s distinctiveness and sociological-origin challenge as well as miracle reports, and explicitly reconnects anchors to the three resurrection facts. Failure to establish miracles is underdetermination, not automatically diversion. Account for full target set before accepting red herring.
